This is a walkthrough for someone who has never opened an OpenGWASDB store
before. Everything below is run from the command line, against the real
pilot stores on this machine, and every output block is pasted verbatim from
an actual run on 2026-08-19 — except the `ogdb info` block in Step 1, re-run
on 2026-08-30 after opengwasdb#114 added the `encoding` line to its output.

If you want the inventory of what exists rather than how to use it, see
[the store catalog](store-catalog.md).

## What is a store, exactly?

A **store** is just a directory. It holds one set of GWAS (or QTL) summary
statistics, plus everything needed to interpret them — no database server, no
central index, nothing to install alongside it. You can copy one to a laptop
and it still works.

Three pieces matter to you as a user:

| Inside the store | What it is |
|---|---|
| `analyses.tsv` | The list of **Analyses** — the GWASes/traits in this store, one per row. Plain TSV; open it in anything. |
| `variants.tsv.gz` | The list of **Variants** — every SNP the store knows about, with position, alleles, rsid. Sorted and tabix-indexed. |
| `data.zarr` | The **associations** themselves (z-scores and standard errors). Compressed arrays; you read these through the CLI, not by hand. |

An **association** is one cell: the effect of one Variant on one Analysis.

Two bits of jargon you'll meet immediately:

- **Analysis** — one GWAS/one trait/one gene's eQTL. Identified by an
  `analysis_id` like `finngen-r13-BMI_IRN` or `GCST009324`.
- **`alid`** — a variant's identifier in the store, formatted
  `chr:position:effect_allele:other_allele`, e.g. `1:1585345:C:T`. **This, not
  the rsid, is what queries take** — see [Gotchas](#gotchas-things-that-will-trip-you-up).

## Setting up

The stores live under `/data/opengwasdb/pilot/`. The `opengwasdb` CLI comes
from this repository's Pixi `dev` environment, so run everything from the
repository root:

```bash
cd /path/to/opengwasdb-stores
pixi run --environment dev opengwasdb --help
```

That prefix gets tedious, so for the rest of this page assume one shell
helper:

```bash
ogdb() { pixi run --environment dev opengwasdb "$@"; }
```

And one store to point at:

```bash
STORE=/data/opengwasdb/pilot/eqtlgen-cis-pilot/releases/pilot-10/store/ragged__eqtlgen-cis-pilot__pilot-10
```

## Step 1 — what am I holding?

Start with `info`. It reads the store's own manifest and tells you what kind
of thing this is:

```bash
ogdb info "$STORE"
```

```
store_id: eqtlgen-cis-pilot
release_id: pilot-10
format_version: 0.1
primary_layout: ragged
association_coverage: cis_and_signals
completion_state: observed_only
reference_assembly: GRCh38
encoding: z=float16, se=float16
```

The four fields worth understanding:

- **`primary_layout`** — `dense`, `ragged`, or `hybrid`. This is a storage
  decision (is the store a full variant × analysis grid, or only selected
  regions?). **You query all three identically**, so mostly you can ignore it.
- **`completion_state`** — `observed_only` means every number came from the
  source GWAS. `reference_completed` means gaps have additionally been
  *imputed* from an LD reference panel. See
  [Observed vs completed](#observed-versus-reference-completed).
- **`association_coverage`** — `full` (genome-wide) versus `cis_and_signals`
  (only regions near the gene of interest, plus significant hits). A
  `cis_and_signals` store genuinely does not contain most of the genome; an
  empty result there means "not stored", not "no effect".
- **`encoding`** — how the z-scores and standard errors are physically stored,
  which is a *precision* statement. The store above reads `z=float16` because
  it is a `format_version` 0.1 release, built before opengwasdb#114. `float16`'s
  spacing widens as |z| grows, so it is least precise exactly where p-values are
  steepest: at |z| = 47.8 the p-value it gives is out by a factor of 1.82.
  Stores rebuilt at `format_version` 1.0 read
  `z=int16_fixed (scale 1/1024), se=float16` — uniform precision, p-values good
  to about 1.6% anywhere, and values too large for the range (up to |z| = 137.5
  in UK Biobank) held exactly in a side table rather than rounded.
  **You query both identically**; only the accuracy of what comes back differs.
  Every store in this catalogue is still 0.1 — rebuilding them is
  opengwasdb#117.

## Step 2 — what's in it?

`analyses.tsv` is a plain TSV, so just read it. It's wide (33 columns), so cut
the ones you care about:

```bash
cut -f2,3,8,9,31 "$STORE/analyses.tsv" | column -t -s$'\t'
```

```
analysis_id                   analysis_label   trait_chr  trait_bp   n_hits_5e8
ENSG00000175445::whole_blood  ENSG00000175445  8          19791998   1071
ENSG00000134243::whole_blood  ENSG00000134243  1          109896382  49
ENSG00000130203::whole_blood  ENSG00000130203  19         45410830   0
ENSG00000073605::whole_blood  ENSG00000073605  17         38068477   2747
ENSG00000164308::whole_blood  ENSG00000164308  5          96233531   3358
ENSG00000232810::whole_blood  ENSG00000232810  6          31544728   1973
ENSG00000141510::whole_blood  ENSG00000141510  17         7577976    67
ENSG00000136244::whole_blood  ENSG00000136244  7          22768562   45
ENSG00000087237::whole_blood  ENSG00000087237  16         57006759   128
ENSG00000136997::whole_blood  ENSG00000136997  8          128750677  69
```

Ten genes' whole-blood cis-eQTLs. The `n_hits_5e8` column is precomputed —
you can see at a glance that ERAP2 (`ENSG00000164308`) and GSDMB
(`ENSG00000073605`) have thousands of genome-wide-significant cis-eQTLs while
APOE (`ENSG00000130203`) has none in this pilot.

::: {.callout-tip}
For a quick sanity check on any store, `cut -f2,3 analyses.tsv` (the ID and
its human-readable label) is almost always what you want.
:::

## Step 3 — your first query

Let's ask for the strongest associations in the store:

```bash
ogdb query-top-hits "$STORE" --limit 5 | column -t -s$'\t'
```

```
analysis_id                   analysis_label   chromosome  position  alid            effect_allele  other_allele  z         se          p         association_status
ENSG00000175445::whole_blood  ENSG00000175445  8           19422641  8:19422641:A:C  A              C             -6.17969  0.0112534   6.42e-10  observed
ENSG00000175445::whole_blood  ENSG00000175445  8           19440256  8:19440256:C:T  C              T             -5.99219  0.0119858   2.07e-09  observed
ENSG00000175445::whole_blood  ENSG00000175445  8           19447574  8:19447574:A:G  A              G             6.35938   0.0123138   2.03e-10  observed
ENSG00000175445::whole_blood  ENSG00000175445  8           19464046  8:19464046:C:T  C              T             6.80859   0.00990295  9.86e-12  observed
ENSG00000175445::whole_blood  ENSG00000175445  8           19465874  8:19465874:C:G  C              G             5.76172   0.00830078  8.33e-09  observed
```

Already readable: five cis-eQTLs for *LPL* (`ENSG00000175445`) on chromosome
8, the strongest at p = 9.9 × 10⁻¹². Every query command resolves and joins
this for you by default now — no separate script, no manual `analyses.tsv`/
`variants.tsv.gz` lookup.

The columns:

- `analysis_id`/`analysis_label` — resolved from `analyses.tsv`.
- `chromosome`/`position`/`alid`/`effect_allele`/`other_allele` — resolved
  from the variant's own `alid` (`chr:pos:effect_allele:other_allele`), so
  these come back essentially for free.
- `z`/`se` — the stored statistics, exactly as before.
- `p` — a two-sided p-value derived from `z`. Past the point a p-value
  underflows float64 (`|z|` beyond ~38, which real GWAS hit — see the
  FADS1/FADS2 example [below](#metabolome-plasma-2023--1400-metabolites-ragged)),
  you'll see `<1e-300` rather than a silently wrong `0`.
- `association_status` — `observed`, `imputed`, or `missing` (ADR-0013). See
  [Observed vs completed](#observed-versus-reference-completed).

Two things are *not* on by default:

- **`rsid`** — pass `--variant-info` to add it (`ogdb query-top-hits "$STORE"
  --limit 5 --variant-info`). It's opt-in because, unlike the columns above,
  resolving it needs an extra lookup against `variants.tsv.gz` that can
  dominate query time on a large result — see
  [Gotchas](#gotchas-things-that-will-trip-you-up).
- **The raw index-keyed form**, for scripts/notebooks that want
  `variant_index`/`analysis_index` rather than resolved identity:

  ```bash
  ogdb query-top-hits "$STORE" --limit 5 --format json
  ```
  ```json
  [{"analysis_index": 0, "se": 0.01125335693359375, "variant_index": 44579, "z": -6.1796875},
   {"analysis_index": 0, "se": 0.01198577880859375, "variant_index": 44652, "z": -5.9921875},
   {"analysis_index": 0, "se": 0.0123138427734375,  "variant_index": 44682, "z": 6.359375},
   {"analysis_index": 0, "se": 0.0099029541015625,  "variant_index": 44750, "z": 6.80859375},
   {"analysis_index": 0, "se": 0.00830078125,       "variant_index": 44762, "z": 5.76171875}]
  ```
  `analysis_index`/`variant_index` are row numbers into `analyses.tsv`/
  `variants.tsv.gz`. This is what every query command returned by default
  before `--format tsv` became the default; `jq` is still the right tool if
  you're consuming this form.

## Step 4 — the five query commands

| Command | Question it answers | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `query-analysis` | "Give me everything for **this one trait**." | store, `analysis_id` |
| `query-phewas` | "What does **this one variant** do, across all traits?" | store, `alid` |
| `query-lookup` | "**These variants** × **these traits**." | store, comma-separated alids, comma-separated analysis_ids |
| `query-range-phewas` | "Everything in **this genomic window**, across all traits." | store, chromosome, start, end |
| `query-top-hits` | "The **strongest** associations." | store, `--threshold`, `--limit` |

All five take the store path first and return the same readable-TSV shape by
default, so every technique below (`cut`, `awk`, `column`) works on any of
them.

### query-analysis

Pull every stored association for one Analysis. These results get large, so
count the data rows first (`tail -n +2` skips the header):

```bash
ogdb query-analysis "$STORE" "ENSG00000136997::whole_blood" | tail -n +2 | wc -l
```

```
7584
```

7,584 cis associations for *MYC*.

### query-phewas

One variant, every Analysis in the store:

```bash
ogdb query-phewas "$STORE" 8:127730605:C:T | column -t -s$'\t'
```

```
analysis_id                   analysis_label   chromosome  position   alid             effect_allele  other_allele  z        se        p         association_status
ENSG00000136997::whole_blood  ENSG00000136997  8           127730605  8:127730605:C:T  C              T             5.85547  0.012764  4.76e-09  observed
```

Only *MYC* comes back — reasonably, since this is a 10-gene store and this
variant is only in *MYC*'s cis window.

### query-top-hits, filtered to one analysis

`query-top-hits` has no per-Analysis flag; it returns hits across the whole
store. Because `analysis_id` is now a real column rather than a row number
you'd have to look up first, filtering to one Analysis is a plain `awk`
match on the text you already know:

```bash
ogdb query-top-hits "$STORE" --threshold 5e-8 \
  | awk -F'\t' 'NR==1 || $1=="ENSG00000136997::whole_blood"' \
  | head -6 | column -t -s$'\t'
```

```
analysis_id                   analysis_label   chromosome  position   alid             effect_allele  other_allele  z         se          p         association_status
ENSG00000136997::whole_blood  ENSG00000136997  8           127730605  8:127730605:C:T  C              T             5.85547   0.012764    4.76e-09  observed
ENSG00000136997::whole_blood  ENSG00000136997  8           127745590  8:127745590:A:G  A              G             5.90625   0.0137634   3.5e-09   observed
ENSG00000136997::whole_blood  ENSG00000136997  8           127801845  8:127801845:A:G  A              G             -6.07031  0.00959778  1.28e-09  observed
ENSG00000136997::whole_blood  ENSG00000136997  8           127841734  8:127841734:C:T  C              T             -5.94141  0.0152359   2.83e-09  observed
ENSG00000136997::whole_blood  ENSG00000136997  8           127891027  8:127891027:G:T  G              T             5.79688   0.0127563   6.76e-09  observed
```

(For one Analysis specifically, `query-analysis` piped through `sort` on the
`p` column, as in the next section's examples, works just as well and skips
the threshold entirely.)

## The four stores, and what each is good for

The four pilot stores deliberately cover different shapes of data. Set
`STORE` to any of these and every command above still works.

### finngen-r13 — disease endpoints (Dense)

20 FinnGen endpoints, genome-wide.

```bash
STORE=/data/opengwasdb/pilot/finngen-r13/releases/r13-pilot-20/store.opengwasdb
cut -f2,3 "$STORE/analyses.tsv" | head -7 | column -t -s$'\t'
```

```
analysis_id                       analysis_label
finngen-r13-BMI_IRN               Body mass index, inverse-rank normalized
finngen-r13-HEIGHT_IRN            Height, inverse-rank normalized
finngen-r13-WEIGHT_IRN            Weight, inverse-rank normalized
finngen-r13-RX_PARACETAMOL_NSAID  Paracetamol or NSAID medication
finngen-r13-K11_ORAL              Diseases of oral cavity, salivary glands and jaws
finngen-r13-FG_CVD                Cardiovascular diseases (excluding rheumatic etc)
```

This is what `query-lookup` is for — one variant across chosen endpoints, in
a single call:

```bash
ogdb query-lookup "$STORE" 1:1585345:C:T \
  finngen-r13-BMI_IRN,finngen-r13-HEIGHT_IRN,finngen-r13-WEIGHT_IRN,finngen-r13-FG_CVD \
  | cut -f1,2,5,8,9,10 | column -t -s$'\t'
```

```
analysis_id             analysis_label                                     alid           z          se          p
finngen-r13-BMI_IRN     Body mass index, inverse-rank normalized           1:1585345:C:T  5.55078    0.00232506  2.84e-08
finngen-r13-HEIGHT_IRN  Height, inverse-rank normalized                    1:1585345:C:T  -0.666992  0.00165462  0.505
finngen-r13-WEIGHT_IRN  Weight, inverse-rank normalized                    1:1585345:C:T  5.14453    0.00216675  2.68e-07
finngen-r13-FG_CVD      Cardiovascular diseases (excluding rheumatic etc)  1:1585345:C:T  2.71094    0.00524902  0.00671
```

A BMI-associated variant that also moves weight (as you'd hope), does
nothing to height, and is only weakly associated with cardiovascular disease.

### gwas-catalog-eur-hybrid — published disease GWAS (Hybrid)

10 European case-control GWAS from the GWAS Catalog. "Hybrid" means the store
splits variants between a shared dense panel and a per-analysis overflow —
invisible at query time:

```bash
STORE=/data/opengwasdb/pilot/gwas-catalog-eur-hybrid/releases/eur-hybrid-pilot-10/store/hybrid__European__pilot10-cc
ogdb query-phewas "$STORE" 1:152220451:C:G | cut -f1,2,8,10 | column -t -s$'\t'
```

```
analysis_id  analysis_label                                                                       z         p
GCST007320   Alzheimer's disease or family history of Alzheimer's disease                         -2.48242  0.013
GCST009324   Parkinson's disease                                                                  7.53516   4.88e-14
GCST009325   Parkinson's disease or first degree relation to individual with Parkinson's disease  7.5       6.38e-14
```

A strong Parkinson's signal that replicates across the two independent
Parkinson's Analyses in the pilot, and is essentially absent elsewhere.

### metabolome-plasma-2023 — 1,400 metabolites (Ragged)

The Chen et al. 2023 plasma metabolome. With this many Analyses,
`query-range-phewas` becomes the interesting one: point it at a locus and ask
what the locus *does*. Here's the FADS1/FADS2 region, a well-known lipid
metabolism hub:

```bash
STORE=/data/opengwasdb/pilot/metabolome-plasma-2023/releases/2023-chen-full-european/store/ragged__pmid-36635386__European
ogdb query-range-phewas "$STORE" 11 61750000 61900000 | tail -n +2 | wc -l
```

```
67316
```

67,316 associations in a 150 kb window. Use `awk` to keep only each
metabolite's single strongest variant (largest `|z|`), then take the top 6 —
`--variant-info` here to get rsids alongside:

```bash
ogdb query-range-phewas "$STORE" 11 61750000 61900000 --variant-info | tail -n +2 \
  | awk -F'\t' '{az=$9<0?-$9:$9; if (az>maxz[$1]) { maxz[$1]=az; row[$1]=$0 } }
                END { for (a in row) print maxz[a]"\t"row[a] }' \
  | sort -t$'\t' -k1,1gr | head -6 | cut -f2- \
  | cut -f1,2,3,6,9,11 | column -t -s$'\t'
```

```
analysis_id   analysis_label                                                                                                     rsid      alid              z         p
GCST90200685  1-stearoyl-2-arachidonoyl-GPC (18:0/20:4) levels                                                                    rs102275  11:61790331:C:T  -47.7812  <1e-300
GCST90200692  1-palmitoyl-2-arachidonoyl-gpc (16:0/20:4n6) levels                                                                 rs102275  11:61790331:C:T  -41.4375  <1e-300
GCST90199788  1-arachidonoyl-gpc (20:4n6) levels                                                                                  rs102275  11:61790331:C:T  -37.7188  <1e-300
GCST90200052  1-(1-enyl-palmitoyl)-2-arachidonoyl-gpc (p-16:0/20:4) levels                                                        rs102275  11:61790331:C:T  -31.2188  5.93e-214
GCST90200794  Oleoyl-linoleoyl-glycerol (18:1 to 18:2) [2] to linoleoyl-arachidonoyl-glycerol (18:2 to 20:4) [1] ratio             rs174564  11:61820833:A:G  -31.0156  3.32e-211
GCST90200740  Arachidonate (20:4n6) to oleate to vaccenate (18:1) ratio                                                           rs174564  11:61820833:A:G  28.4688   2.86e-178
```

Every top metabolite is arachidonate-containing, and the lead variants
(rs102275, rs174564) are the canonical FADS variants — the store reproduces
textbook biology in one command. Note the `p` column: `-47.78` is well past
the point a two-sided p-value underflows float64 (~`|z|` = 38), so instead of
a silently wrong `0` you get an explicit `<1e-300`.

## Observed versus reference-completed {#observed-versus-reference-completed}

Some stores ship a second, `-completed` release alongside the original. That
release has had missing cells **imputed** from an LD reference panel. The
difference is visible immediately:

```bash
EQ=/data/opengwasdb/pilot/eqtlgen-cis-pilot/releases/pilot-10/store
ogdb query-analysis "$EQ/ragged__eqtlgen-cis-pilot__pilot-10"           "ENSG00000136997::whole_blood" | tail -n +2 | wc -l
ogdb query-analysis "$EQ/ragged__eqtlgen-cis-pilot__pilot-10-completed" "ENSG00000136997::whole_blood" | tail -n +2 | wc -l
```

```
7584
18988
```

Same gene, 2.5× the associations. The extra 11,404 are **statistical
inferences, not measurements** — and the readable output tells you which is
which, via the `association_status` column, with no extra flag needed:

```bash
ogdb query-analysis "$EQ/ragged__eqtlgen-cis-pilot__pilot-10-completed" "ENSG00000136997::whole_blood" \
  | tail -n +2 | cut -f11 | sort | uniq -c
```

```
   4356 imputed
   7048 missing
   7584 observed
```

::: {.callout-note}
`association_status` is `observed`, `imputed`, or `missing` on every row, in
both the default TSV and `--format json`. If you only want measured values,
filter on it (`awk -F'\t' '$11=="observed"'`) or query the `observed_only`
release instead.
:::

## Gotchas — things that will trip you up {#gotchas}

**Queries take `alid`, not rsid.** This is the big one. Every store here has
an empty variant-alias table, so passing an rsid returns nothing at all — not
an error, just an empty result (a header line and nothing else) you could
easily misread as "no association":

```bash
STORE=/data/opengwasdb/pilot/eqtlgen-cis-pilot/releases/pilot-10/store/ragged__eqtlgen-cis-pilot__pilot-10
ogdb query-phewas "$STORE" rs16902359         # -> header only
ogdb query-phewas "$STORE" 8:127730605:C:T    # -> the association
```

To go from an rsid to its `alid`, scan the store's variant table (column 7 is
the rsid, column 6 the `alid`):

```bash
MET=/data/opengwasdb/pilot/metabolome-plasma-2023/releases/2023-chen-full-european/store/ragged__pmid-36635386__European
zcat "$MET/variants.tsv.gz" | awk -F'\t' '$7=="rs174564" {print $6; exit}'
```

```
11:61820833:A:G
```

If you already know the position, `tabix` is instant and avoids the scan:

```bash
tabix "$STORE/variants.tsv.gz" 8:127730605-127730605
```

```
8	127730605	55565	C	T	8:127730605:C:T	rs16902359	.
```

**Allele order matters in an `alid`.** It is
`chr:pos:effect_allele:other_allele`. `8:127730605:C:T` and
`8:127730605:T:C` are different keys, and the sign of `z` follows the effect
allele.

**An empty result may mean "not stored".** In a `cis_and_signals` store
(`eqtlgen-cis-pilot`, `metabolome-plasma-2023`), most of the genome was
never stored. Check `association_coverage` in `ogdb info` before concluding
there's no effect.

**Not every store has rsids, and rsid isn't returned unless you ask.** Pass
`--variant-info` to add the `rsid` column. FinnGen and the GWAS Catalog
hybrid stores have no rsid for any variant — shown as `.` (the Store Variant
Table's own missing marker), same as an individual variant with no rsid in a
store that otherwise has them:

```bash
ogdb query-lookup "$STORE" 1:1585345:C:T finngen-r13-BMI_IRN --variant-info | tail -n +2 | cut -f3
```

```
.
```

**`trait_bp` in `eqtlgen-cis-pilot` is on the source build.** The store's
variants are GRCh38, but `analyses.tsv`'s `trait_chr`/`trait_bp` carry the
hg19 coordinates from the source BESD files (the manifest records
`source_build: hg19`). *MYC* is listed at `8:128750677` (hg19) while its own
cis-eQTLs sit around 127.7–127.9 Mb (hg38). Don't mix the two when defining
a window.

**Store paths are not uniform.** Each family lays its releases out slightly
differently — `.../store.opengwasdb` for FinnGen, `.../store/<name>` for the
others. Use tab-completion, or copy the paths from
[the store catalog](store-catalog.md).
